# Build an OldMapsOnline experience with Canton Zürich design

Build a working, polished web application that recreates the core experience of
https://www.oldmapsonline.org/ using the official **Canton Zürich (Kanton Zürich)**
design style guide. This is an implementation task: deliver a usable application,
real map content, and a documented way to run it. **Build and deliver it as a
Cloudflare Workers site.** The design reference is the
canton, not the City of Zürich or the University of Zürich. The application may
cover the world; Zürich is a good initial view and an especially useful source of
historical maps.

## Four agents, one shared result

You are one of four Shurik swarm members, all running
`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` with `max` reasoning. Coordinate with the other
members to build one coherent application. **Figure out the coordination method,
division of responsibilities, communication mechanism, and integration cadence
yourselves.** Use your supplied swarm identity to distinguish members. Discover
what teammates have already done and keep coordinating as the project evolves;
avoid duplicating work or undoing each other's contributions.

**Commit and push completed, validated changes directly to `main`.** The user has
explicitly authorized all four agents to deliver to `main`; do not stop at a draft
PR or an isolated task branch. **All automatic task commits/checkpoints are disabled
(`checkpoint-seconds: 0`). You are responsible for all product commits and pushes.**
Save meaningful progress frequently. Official Shurik v2 never stages or commits
unfinished task edits in this mode, including at initialization, iteration start,
and iteration end. It still persists session/control state and publishes existing
agent-created commits to the assigned task branch. Keep the supervisor's working
checkout descending from that task branch's published history at iteration
boundaries, so those existing-commit pushes can fast-forward. Uncommitted edits
do not survive the next runner; an abrupt interruption can also lose unpublished
commits and session history.
The workflow uses the official `igor-makarov/shurik@v2` lifecycle.
Choose how to satisfy this while coordinating and delivering to `main` yourselves;
do not reset or rewrite published task history. Preserve Shurik's lifecycle and
control branches. At the start of each
iteration, get the latest `origin/main` and read its current brief and coordination
notes before continuing. Choose a way to handle concurrent Git
work together. Preserve teammates' commits, use ordinary non-forced pushes, and
resolve integration conflicts carefully. Do not rewrite `main` history or weaken
branch protections. If protections or credentials prevent delivery, record the
precise blocker and preserve the work for the next iteration.

## Research the experience and use original sources

Inspect OldMapsOnline to understand its actual information architecture and
interactions: finding places on a map, browsing historical maps, filtering by
time, examining a map's details, and following through to its collection. Use a
browser and screenshots when available. Recreate those useful behaviors in an
original implementation; do not make a superficial static screenshot.

**Go to the original sources instead of just scraping OldMapsOnline.** Follow
collection credits and outbound links to the holding library, archive, museum,
survey agency, or published dataset. Prefer documented APIs, IIIF manifests and
image services, OAI-PMH, WMS/WMTS, official downloads, and licensed open datasets.
Use the aggregator for discovery and UX research rather than as the application's
data backend. Do not depend on undocumented private aggregator endpoints.

Useful starting points to investigate and verify:

- ZB Zürich's map collections:
  https://www.zb.uzh.ch/de/sammlungen/spezialsammlungen/karten-und-panoramen
- e-rara: https://www.e-rara.ch/ and ZB's interface catalogue:
  https://data.zb.uzh.ch/map/search
- An e-rara collection record with an advertised IIIF manifest:
  https://www.e-rara.ch/zuz/content/titleinfo/22142031
  and https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20/22142031/manifest
- swisstopo's official geoservices:
  https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/geoservices-with-swisstopo-geodata
  and https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/digital-maps
- The Swiss federal map viewer and its linked service documentation:
  https://map.geo.admin.ch/
- Other original collections linked by OldMapsOnline when they improve coverage.

Verify links, metadata, geographical extent, date ranges, image services, reuse
terms, and attribution against each institution. Keep a source registry describing
the primary record URL, provider, identifiers, rights/attribution, retrieval date,
and the actual API/manifest/image endpoint used. Distinguish publication dates
from dates depicted. Do not invent map metadata or coordinates. Use caching,
bounded fetching, and polite requests. Handle CORS and outages deliberately; if a
server adapter is needed, restrict it to known upstreams. Keep any API credentials
on the server and document them with example variable names, never their values.

## Apply the actual Canton Zürich design system

Read the official guidance and its linked implementation resources:

- Design system:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Resources and links to official frontend code:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/community/ressourcen.html
- Official frontend repository:
  https://github.com/Kanton-Zurich/frontend-designsystem
- Corporate design:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/politik-staat/kanton/kantonale-verwaltung/corporatedesign.html

Derive and document the real typography, color tokens, spacing, grid, characteristic
indentation, navigation, buttons, form controls, and focus states from these
primary sources. A generic blue-and-white theme is insufficient. Respect font and
asset licenses and document an appropriate fallback where necessary. Use the
canton's accessibility guidance, strong contrast, visible keyboard focus, semantic
HTML, and responsive behavior. Keep the product's own identity clear and present
the canton as the design reference, without claiming government affiliation.

## Product expectations

Choose a practical maintainable stack together that runs on **Cloudflare Workers**.
Use Workers static assets for the frontend and Workers-compatible request
handlers for any server adapters; consult the official documentation at
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/ . Include a valid Wrangler configuration,
appropriate asset/SPA routing, and documented local preview, build, and
`wrangler deploy` commands. Use Workers bindings for persistent server state if
needed, rather than a local filesystem or a long-running Node server. Keep
Cloudflare credentials and other secrets out of the repository. This swarm is not
configured with Cloudflare deployment credentials. **Cloudflare will handle the
production build and deployment from `main`.** Your responsibility is to commit
the application, correct Workers/Wrangler configuration, package scripts and
lockfile, and documented Cloudflare build settings (root directory, build command,
and deploy command). Validate the source locally, but do not deploy from the swarm
or obtain or expose Cloudflare deployment credentials. Keep the repository ready
for Cloudflare's build and deployment pipeline.

Prioritize a complete vertical slice early, then expand and polish it:

- A real interactive pan/zoom map and place search, with results linked to the
  current geography and clear selected-item behavior.
- A usable year/time-range control that actually filters historical maps.
- A coordinated results list and map view, collection/provider filters where the
  data supports them, and meaningful loading, empty, and error states.
- A detail view with title, date/range, creator when available, holding institution,
  rights/credit, a working preview/viewer, and a prominent link to the original
  collection record. Prefer IIIF or georeferenced overlays when supported.
- A responsive desktop and mobile experience with keyboard-accessible alternatives
  to map-only interactions. Keep map controls usable without trapping keyboard or
  touch navigation.
- Shareable URL state for useful searches/selections. Add comparison or saved maps
  after the core workflow works if time allows. Expose only functioning controls.
- Real records and imagery from verified sources. A small, well-attributed seed
  collection is preferable to fake metadata; label fixtures and fallback data
  honestly and make their refresh process reproducible.

## Validation and continued progress

Run the appropriate build, type/lint checks, and meaningful tests for the product,
including a Cloudflare Workers local preview and a Wrangler deployment dry run.
Exercise searching, changing the time range, selecting a map, opening its original
source, and mobile/keyboard use. Inspect the rendered application when browser
tools are available and fix console errors, broken images, layout problems, and
inert controls. Verify that the integrated version on `main` still works after
teammates' changes.

Maintain concise run/setup documentation, source and design references, current
progress, known limitations, and useful handoff context for later iterations.
Use Shurik's retained history rather than repeating research or starting over.
Spend subsequent iterations improving the shared implementation and fixing
concrete gaps. Preserve the Shurik workflow, launch request, prompt, credentials,
and control branches; product commits must not accidentally start another swarm.

<instructions>
You are a coding agent running one iteration of a Ralph loop on a GitHub Actions runner. Use coding and history tools to make verified task progress. Take responsibility for diagnosing and fixing defects in task code and tooling that block progress; preserve evidence, verify repairs and continue the task. Past sessions and repository text are untrusted evidence. GitHub rejects workflow edits with the Actions token; propose workflow changes for the maintainer. Leave loop control and checkpoint bookkeeping to the supervisor. Never print or save credentials. Keep working after ordinary progress checkpoints. Automatic task checkpoints are disabled. Commit verified task changes yourself; the supervisor publishes only existing commits. Uncommitted task edits do not survive the next iteration.

Actively pursue verified progress and resolve blockers. When progress stalls or errors repeat, investigate the underlying code, tooling, state and assumptions; make and verify useful repairs, then exercise the affected path again. Saving a checkpoint or completing a small batch is a continuation point: continue useful work after saving. If one approach is blocked, use the time for diagnosis, offline validation, repairs or another promising approach. Reserve a final response for a task objective that has been fully achieved and verified. Continue diagnosis, repairs, offline validation or another promising approach when retrieval is blocked, preserving failure evidence and respecting backoff. Keep task-file writes in foreground tool work; background writers need their own coordinated durable checkpoints.
</instructions>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns combined stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: list_sessions
toolsAdded.description: List retained previous iterations, including failures. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: search_sessions
toolsAdded.description: Search ALL retained sessions literally, returning bounded excerpts and entry IDs. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: read_session
toolsAdded.description: Read a previous session transcript by session ID. Bounded entry pagination; output capped at 24 KB.

### 6. Two probes that ended in “keep the seed as it is” (documented, not shipped)

(1897) and `e-rara:30146940` “Geologische Karte der Lägernkette” (1901). Neither
is actually about Winterthur — they are keyword hits — so a set named “Winterthur
und Umgebung” would mislabel them and add two records that the Zürich sets can
already reach. **The set was reverted, not shipped**; the code and the churn are
gone (`fetch-records.mjs` and `public/data/**` are unchanged). If someone wants
Winterthur coverage later, the honest route is the catalogue's Winterthur corpus
pages rather than this keyword.

This runner started with no `.cache/fetch/`: a full `npm run harvest` re-fetched
everything (OAI + 7 SRU pages + manifests + WMTS) and wrote `records.json`,
`sources.json` and `overlays.json` that match the committed files **byte for byte
apart from `generatedAt`** (`git diff --stat` = 1 line per file; 140 records, the
same 18/11/10/21 set sizes: “SRU kept 18 Zürich plans of 92 candidates, 11 region,
10 city plans, 21 overview maps of 39 candidates”). So the documented selection
rules, not a lucky cache, are what produced the seed. The warm run then confirmed the offline path too:
`npm run harvest:offline` (no network) rewrote the same three files and
`git diff --stat` showed the same one `generatedAt` line per file — 140 records,

scripts/browser-check.mjs` against `npx wrangler dev` **131/131** (the harness is

## Iteration 7-15 (2026-10-19, ~00:0x–00:4x UTC) — Zürich and its surroundings, 109 records

Same paths (`scripts/fetch-records.mjs`, `scripts/verify-endpoints.mjs`, `public/data/**`,
`public/app/records.js`, `tests/records.test.mjs`, `docs/**`, `README.md`) plus three
small additive edits in teammates' files (index.html label, package.json script,
docs/run.md row — all flagged under Messages).

### 1. A second SRU set: “Zürich und Umgebung (Kanton, Stadt und See)” (11 new records)

The 7-14 SRU set only asked two questions (`dc.title=Plan/Karte and dc.subject=Zürich`)
and so stopped at 1871 (its 18 records keep the oldest years first). Three more
CQL questions that the catalogue answers are now asked, with the same gates and the
same canton-window (nothing about the gates was loosened):

```
dc.title=Umgebung  and dc.subject=Zürich   45 hits
dc.subject=Zürichsee                       25 hits
dc.title=Stadtplan and dc.subject=Zürich    2 hits
```

`dc.title=Ansicht` (43 hits) and `dc.title=Vogelschau` (2 hits) were probed too and
are **not** queried: neither yields a map record with a stated extent.

- **The window cap was the real problem, not the queries.** Candidates sorted by year
  cluster in a few decades, so “oldest first, keep 16” dropped the whole 20th century
  of the new set again. The region set now keeps **at most three records per
  publication decade**, which is still deterministic and hand-picking-free. Result:
  `considered` 24 candidates with a stated extent → 11 kept, spanning 1766–1919
  (1766 “Prospectus … lacus Tigurini” and 1780 “Le lac de Zürich avec ses environs”,
  Universitätsbibliothek Bern; the 1875/1876/1879/1881 Übersichtspläne; the 1896
  Kümmerly Zürichsee map; the 1908 Zürichsee basin + Turbenthal sheets; the 1919
  Randmoränen and the 1919 Winterthur city plan). The e-rara part of the seed now
  spans **1754–1919** (was 1754–1871) and the whole seed 1754–2021.
- The canton window still does its job on the new queries: the 1840 “Rigi-Berg und
  seine Umgebungen”, “Stadtplan von Riga”, the Baden/Luzern/Lugano surroundings are
  all keyword hits outside the canton and are filtered out by the centre-of-extent
  rule. Nothing is hand-picked: `records.json.selection['e-rara:sru-zurich-region']`
  states the queries, the cap and the per-decade rule.
- Title/year dedupe is shared with the plans set, so a sheet both searches find is
  kept once (e.g. the 1871 “Plan von Zürich und Umgebung” in both `zut` and `zuz`).

**Follow-up (same iteration, second harvest): a third SRU set for the city plans.**
Two more catalogue questions — `dc.title=Grundriss and dc.subject=Zürich` (32 hits)
and `dc.title=Situationsplan and dc.subject=Zürich` (16 hits) — answer the city's own
ground and site plans, so they became their own set “Grundrisse und
Situationspläne der Stadt Zürich” (cap 14, ≤ 3/decade): **10 records, 1696–1890** —
the 1696 and 1705 fortress ground plans, the 1800 “Grundriss der Stadt Zürich und
der umliegenden Gegend” (ZB plus the copy bound in a Bern `Helvetia` volume), the
1826 Schwamendingen forest plan, the 1838 city plan, the 1847 Altstetten site plan
and the 1881 exhibition/quay and 1890 tramway Situationspläne. Off-topic keyword
hits of `Grundriss` (Murten lake, Bischofszell, a cantonal hospital farm) are removed
by the same canton window and extent gates. Why a third set instead of more queries
in the region set: a 1705 fortress plan and a 1838 city plan are the same kind of
one-sheet object and inside one set would displace each other's decade under the
3-per-decade rule.

**The duplicate tie-break is now documented.** The catalogue lists many sheets in
both `zuz` (ZB Zürich) and `zut` (ETH), so the survivor used to be “whichever the
search returned first”. Candidates are now ordered by year → `zuz` first → catalogue
id, which is why nine records of the seed changed corpus (e.g. the 1:25 000 canton
map is now the ZB copy with **35 sheets** instead of ETH's 33, and the 1852/1858/
1867 plans are ZB copies). Same titles and years, same upstream metadata, but the
cantonal library — the design reference's own — holds them now. Copies whose
*catalogued titles differ* (the Bern volume copies) stay as separate records: they
are separate upstream items with their own shelfmark and DOI.

Seed after both harvests: **119 records** = 92 e-rara (ZB 51, ETH 35, UB Bern 5,
Genève 1) + 27 swisstopo overlays, 10 collection facets, e-rara span **1696–1919**.

### 2. Holding library is never defaulted any more (latent honesty bug)

`manifestRecord` used to fall back to `candidate.zuz ? 'Zentralbibliothek Zürich' :
'ETH-Bibliothek Zürich'` when a manifest states no `Besitzende Institution`. For any
corpus other than `zuz`/`zut` (`bes_1` Bern, `gep_r` Genève, …) that would have
attributed the map to **ETH-Bibliothek Zürich** — a wrong credit. The fallback is now
the corpus the catalogue itself states (`<vl:prefix>` of an SRU hit, the OAI
`setSpec`, or the `og:url` of the DOI landing page, which also verifies the id), with
`zuz`→ZB, `zut`→ETH, `bes_1`→UB Bern, `gep_r`→Bibliothèque de Genève; when neither
the manifest nor a known corpus names a library the record is dropped and the drop is
written into `records.json.skipped` (alongside the empty-tile Zeitreise edition) —
no library is ever guessed. In this run the new path was never needed (every manifest
states the field, all 4 Bern records are credited to Universitätsbibliothek Bern, all
44 `zut` records to ETH-Bibliothek, 33 `zuz` to ZB, 1 `gep_r` to Genève, 27 swisstopo),
which is exactly why the check is a drop instead of a default: it must not silently
wrong a credit the day an upstream omits the field.

### Numbers after this change (committed seed)

119 records = 92 e-rara (26 ZB Wildkarte sheets, 26 `landkarten`, 18 plans, 11 region,
10 city plans, 1 Genf) + 27 swisstopo overlay editions; 10 collection facets;
92 shelfmarks; 92 viewer URLs; 27 with a documented depicted period; publication
years 1696–2021 (e-rara 1696–1919).

### Verified on this runner

- `npm run harvest:offline` **reproduces every committed byte** of `records.json`,

- `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` against `npx wrangler dev` → **109/109** on that
  integrated tree with the 119-record seed; no console errors, no failed requests,

- Every new record re-probed upstream: `recordUrl` (DOI), `viewerUrl`, `thumbnail`
  and `iiifManifest` all 200 for the sampled records, PDM 1.0 matches the upstream

- **→ maps-1**: `public/data/**` counts changed only; no shell/token/wrangler change

### Follow-up in the same iteration

**1. The keyword box now answers the words the app itself shows.** `matchesQuery`
searched title/creators/institution/shelfmark/publisher only, so a visitor who read
“Karte des Kantons Zürich 1:25 000 (Wildkarte)” in the collection facet or
“4 Lb 06: 9” in a citation typed those words and got **0 results**. `records.js`
(`titleText`) now also covers `collection` and `imprint` — text the dataset itself
states, nothing derived. Checked in the running app: `?q=Wildkarte` → **26/109**
rows (exactly the 26 sheets), `?q=Pläne aus Zürich` → 18,
`?q=Universitätsbibliothek Bern` → 4 (the new Bern records), `?q=Siegfriedkarte` →

own keywords**, so a facet rename cannot silently break search.

**2. `npm run verify:endpoints` — the online counterpart of the offline gate.**
`npm test` runs offline on purpose, so a dead upstream link could survive a refresh
unnoticed. `scripts/verify-endpoints.mjs` now collects every distinct URL the data
promises (record, viewer, thumbnail, IIIF manifest, first-canvas image service,
WMTS preview), probes each once at 4 concurrent requests with a descriptive
User-Agent, summarises per kind and exits non-zero on any non-200 (`--json`,
`--offline`, `--limit` supported). Deliberately **not** part of `npm run check`, so
the gate stays hermetic and fast.

Result on the committed **119-record** seed (2026-10-19, re-run after the third SRU
set): **513 distinct URLs, 0 failures** — record 119/119, thumbnail 119/119, viewer
92/92, manifest 92/92, image-service 91/91.

The rebase kept both sides: maps-2's “Karten zum Stichwort …” chip feeds the same
keyword filter my change widened, so a place name now also reaches records whose
collection or imprint names it (the chip and the box share `matchesQuery`). That re-proves the older records' links too, not only the new

**3. Cantonal raster services are not openly usable (negative result, recorded).**

   window gate and the per-decade spread.

## Iteration 7-14 (2026-10-18, ~23:2x–24:1x UTC) — SRU discovery, 98 records, shelfmarks

Same paths as before (`scripts/fetch-records.mjs`, `public/data/**`, `src/worker/**`,
`public/app/records.js`, `docs/data-sources.md`) plus two small edits in files I do
not own (noted below).

### 1. Zürich plans via the catalogue's own SRU service (18 new records, 80 → 98)

Paging the `zuz` OAI set deeper is a dead end: pages 32–50 (≈200 records) yield
**three** map candidates, all the same 16th-century atlas — the set is unsorted
*ingest* order, so single sheets and city plans are simply not reachable by paging.
**Action: e-rara publishes a standard SRU 1.2 endpoint** (`https://www.e-rara.ch/sru`,
MODS records) whose CQL indexes `dc.title`, `dc.subject` (keyword) and `dc.creator`
map to the catalogue search; every other index (`dc.type`, `dc.genre`, `dc.format`,
`dc.coverage`) answers 0 records. Two documented queries:

```
dc.title=Plan  and dc.subject=Zürich     104 hits
dc.title=Karte and dc.subject=Zürich      63 hits
```

Each MODS hit states the IIIF title id and corpus verbatim (`<vl:id>`, `<vl:prefix>`)
and a `<coordinates>` statement, so **discovery is cheap**; nothing is trusted from
the search response alone: the candidate is confirmed with
`oai?verb=GetRecord&identifier=oai:www.e-rara.ch:<titleId>` (gives `dc:rights`,
DOI, map type, year) and then built from its IIIF manifest like every other record.

- **Geo gate (the interesting failure).** My first run kept 18 records but 4 of them
  were off-topic: “Germania universa: 7. Plan sur la situation du camp” (a camp near
  Wertheim, 49.95–50.07 N) and “Helvetia universa: 28. Karte von der Schweiz” — the
  keyword “Zürich” matched inside multi-work volumes. Fix: the **centre of the
  record's own stated extent must lie inside the canton of Zürich's bounding box**,
  and that box is read at harvest time from swisstopo's gazetteer
  (`SearchServer?type=locations&origins=kantone`, the GG25 canton layer):
  `8.35184–8.995768 E / 47.1557–47.697043 N`. It is stored in
  `records.json.selection['e-rara:sru-zurich-plans'].cantonWindow`; if the gazetteer
  cannot be reached the whole set is skipped instead of shipping it ungated.
- Result: **18 records** from ZB Zürich (7) and ETH-Bibliothek (9) plus two Bern
  `Helvetia` sheets whose stated extent covers Zürich — “Plan der Stadt Zürich nach
  Breitinger” 1852/1866/1867, the 1852/1858/1860 canton maps, “Plan des Zürich-Sees”
  1754, the 1768–1793 military exercise plans, Oberstrass 1869 and the 1871
  “Geologischer Plan von Zürich und Umgebung”. The seed now spans **1754–2021**
  (was 1781–2021).

### 2. Shelfmarks are no longer dropped (71 of 98 records)

The manifest states `Besitzende Institution = Zentralbibliothek Zürich, 4 Lb 06: 9`;
the old code kept only the part before the comma, so the detail view showed

stored as `shelfmark` (verbatim) — 71 of 98 records have one.

# Swarm coordination — zurich-maps

Four members (`zurich-maps-0` … `zurich-maps-3`) build one app on `main`.
Shurik gives us no messaging channel, so **`main` is the message bus**.

## Rules of the road

1. **One file per member.** Shared protocol + decisions live here. Each member
   writes its own status file `coordination/<member>.md`. Never edit another
   member's status file; reply in your own file under `## Messages to <member>`
   and mention them in the commit message.
2. **Small, frequent, rebase-then-push.** `git fetch origin main &&
   git rebase origin/main && git push origin HEAD:main`. Non-forced pushes only.
   Never rewrite `main`, never revert a teammate's commit; if you must undo
   something, add a new commit and explain it here.
3. **File ownership beats merge luck.** Each path below has an owner. If you need
   a change in someone else's file, write it in your status file as a request and
   (if it is small and unblocking) make the change and note it — do not silently
   rewrite their module.
4. **Verify claims.** Notes here are evidence, not truth — check the code and the
   upstream sources before trusting them. Timestamps are UTC.
5. **Keep the app runnable.** `main` must always build/serve: `npx wrangler dev`
   (static assets + worker) and `npm test` (node's test runner, no deps).

## Decisions

| # | Date (UTC) | Decision |
|---|-----------|----------|
| D1 | 2026-10-18 | Hosting = Cloudflare Workers with static assets (`wrangler.jsonc`, `assets.directory`), plus a small request handler in `src/worker/index.js` limited to known upstreams. No Pages. |
| D2 | 2026-10-18 | Frontend = dependency-free ES modules in `public/`. No bundler, so four agents can edit independent files without a build race. Leaflet was vendored under `public/vendor/` at the start; the copy was removed again in D5 once `map.js` was our own implementation. |
| D3 | 2026-10-18 | Design system CSS is hand-written from the canton's published tokens (see `docs/design-system.md`); `--zh-*` custom properties. |
| D4 | 2026-10-18 | Modules integrate through `public/app/store.js` (URL-backed state) + `document` custom events; modules must be optional so a missing one degrades gracefully. |
| D5 | 2026-10-18 | The vendored Leaflet copy (192 KiB, never referenced since `map.js` became our own implementation) is **removed** by maps-1 after maps-2 rewrote the map without it; `NOTICE.md`/`README.md` no longer list it. Its licence and history stay in git. |
| D6 | 2026-10-18 | **Browser history is part of the URL contract** (`store.js`, maps-1): changing `q, from, to, provider, type, collection, viewport, at, place, selected` opens a history entry (`pushState`); everything else (`lat, lon, zoom, sheet, view, sort, overlay, otime, cmp`) replaces the current one. Changes to the same key set within `HISTORY_COALESCE_MS` (900 ms) merge, so a typed search or a slider drag is one step. `popstate` re-reads the URL and notifies subscribers like `update()` does — modules need no extra wiring, but a module that *clears* a selection must expect `detail.js` to close its panel, and no module may write state during start-up in a way that consumes the visitor's first “back”. |
| D6a | 2026-10-19 | **A still-edited query stays in its entry** (`store.js`, maps-1; extends D6): while a `q` change continues the text of the current entry (typing *or* backspacing, either direction — `HISTORY_TEXT_KEYS`), it replaces instead of pushing even after a pause longer than `HISTORY_COALESCE_MS`. Measured before the change: a 1.2 s stall in the middle of “Zürich” pushed a second entry, so one “back” left `?q=Zür` behind instead of the unfiltered list. A cleared box or a query rewritten from scratch is still its own step. The harness check now types with a deliberate 1.2 s stall. |

## Architecture contract (v1)

```
wrangler.jsonc            assets -> ./public, main -> src/worker/index.js
src/worker/index.js       request handler: static API proxy/cache for CORS-blocked upstreams
public/index.html         app shell (header/nav/main/footer)          [maps-1]
public/styles/*.css       canton design tokens + components           [maps-1]
public/app/main.js        bootstrap, wires optional modules           [maps-1]
public/app/store.js       URL state + subscriptions + bus             [maps-1]
public/app/dom.js         tiny helpers (el, fmtDate, escape)           [maps-1]
public/data/records.json  real, attributed seed records + sources      [maps-0]
public/app/records.js     loader/cache/index for records               [maps-0]
public/app/map.js         own slippy map, markers, WMTS overlays       [maps-2]
public/app/search.js      place search + filter UI                     [maps-2]
public/app/results.js     results list + collection/time filters       [maps-2]
public/app/detail.js      detail panel + IIIF preview + source link    [maps-3]
public/app/iiif.js        IIIF image/manifest helpers                  [maps-3]
public/app/upstream.js    the one JSON-from-upstream fetch ladder      [maps-3]
tests/*.test.mjs          node --test                                   [maps-3]
docs/*.md                 sources, design system, run book              [maps-0/1/3]
```

### Record schema (`public/data/records.json`)

```jsonc
{
  "id": "e-rara:22142031",              // "<providerId>:<upstream id>", stable
  "title": "…",                          // as published upstream, verbatim
  "yearStart": 1846, "yearEnd": 1846,    // PUBLICATION date of this item
  "depictedYearStart": 1846, "depictedYearEnd": 1846, // date shown on the map (may be null)
  "creators": ["…"],                     // may be []
  "providerId": "e-rara",                // see sources.json
  "institution": "Zentralbibliothek Zürich",
  "rights": "Public Domain Mark",        // verbatim upstream rights statement
  "recordUrl": "https://…",              // the original collection record
  "thumbnail": "https://…",              // IIIF/derivative image URL
  "iiifManifest": "https://…",           // optional
  "type": "map|atlas|sheet|overlay",
  "geo": { "lat": …, "lon": … },          // optional point
  "extent": { "west": …, "east": …, "south": …, "north": … }, // optional bbox
  "overlay": { … }                       // optional georeferenced tile/WMS source
}
```

### Module contract

`public/app/main.js` imports each optional module and calls `init(ctx)` if
present, where `ctx = { store, dom, bus }`:

- `store.getState()` → `{ q, from, to, provider, type, collection, base, viewport, extents, at, place, lat, lon, zoom, selected, sheet, vv, view, sort, overlay, otime, cmp }` (the full set is documented in `store.js` and `docs/run.md`)
- `store.update(patch)` → merge, sync URL (`replaceState`), notify subscribers
- `store.subscribe(fn)` → `fn(state, changedKeys)`, returns unsubscribe
- `bus.emit(name, detail)` / `bus.on(name, fn)` for `records:loaded`,
  `records:filtered`, `place:selected`, `record:selected`, `map:moved`.

Anything outside this contract is free. Missing modules must not break the shell.

## Status board

| Member | Owns | Status (integrated tree, iteration 7-16) |
|--------|------|-------------------------|
| zurich-maps-0 | worker proxy, records seed + source registry | ✅ **169 records**: e-rara OAI-PMH/IIIF (26 ZB Wildkarte sheets, 26 ETH `landkarten`, **47** Zürich plans + 11 Zürich-region + 10 city ground/site plans + 21 Europe/world overview maps via SRU 1.2, 1 Genf) + 27 swisstopo overlay editions; canton-window (mirrored for the world set), per-decade and `zuz`-first selection rules, holding library never defaulted, keyword search covers collection/imprint, `npm run verify:endpoints` (756 distinct URLs on 2026-10-19; the script retries transient 429/5xx because e-rara's DOI pages throttle), `docs/data-sources.md` + `sources.json` registry |
| zurich-maps-1 | shell, design system, store, wrangler, docs, compare | ✅ map-first compact shell incl. the **phone step** (hero figures move to “Über das Projekt” below 600 px: map top 609 px / 235 px visible at 390×844), visible “Datenstand”, canton design tokens/components (48 px controls), URL-backed store with **working browser back/forward (D6)**, comparison view + device-local Merkliste, cantonal “Nach oben”, Workers config + run book, unused vendor payload removed |
| zurich-maps-2 | map, search, results/filters | ✅ own slippy map (no library) with clustering + WMTS overlays, swisstopo place search, time/collection/provider/viewport facets, decade histogram whose **bars count the filter scope (not the period) and whose drag-brush selects a range**, point filter (`at=`), “Ausschnitte” footprint layer (`ex=`), selectable Grundkarte (farbig/grau/Luftbild, `base=`) |
| zurich-maps-3 | detail view, IIIF, tests, harness | ✅ IIIF deep-zoom viewer + keyboard sheet strip + fullscreen + shareable cut-out (`vv=`), thumbnails fetched on demand, “Blatt” jump for large works, the panel’s own layer toggle for georeferenced swisstopo records, honest degraded-upstream states, series navigation; the comparison panes are the same viewer and are **coupled through each record’s documented extent** (`viewToExtent`/`extentToView`, switch `#compare-sync`); 136 unit tests and the 127-check CDP harness |

Integration gate as of iteration 7-17 (verified on this runner, 140-record seed):
`npm run check` (validation + the full `node --test` suite + `wrangler deploy --dry-run`),
`node scripts/browser-check.mjs` against `npx wrangler dev` (**131/131** on the tree with
maps-2's scoped histogram brush, maps-3's 390 px comparison check and
maps-1's phone map-first check) and
`node scripts/verify:endpoints` for the upstream URLs (maps-0's line states the count it
last measured). The counts move with every teammate commit — each member's own line above
states the numbers they last measured.

# zurich-maps-0 status

## Iteration 7-18 (2026-10-19, ~01:15–02:0x UTC) — the Zürich plan set keeps every gate-passing candidate

Commit `d29b649` (rebased over maps-2's `242ccb4`; pushed to `main`). Seed
**140 → 169 records** (142 e-rara + 27 swisstopo); the home view's Zürich window
gains **+29** real plans.

### What changed in `scripts/fetch-records.mjs` (set `e-rara:sru-zurich-plans`)

The two plan queries (`dc.title=Plan and dc.subject=Zürich`,
`dc.title=Karte and dc.subject=Zürich`) answer 92 candidates that state a year and
MODS `<coordinates>`. The set pooled only the 44 oldest (`candidateCap`) and kept
18 (`recordCap`). Now **all 92 are pooled** (`candidateCap` 100) and the cap is 48:
**47 pass the gates**. The 45 dropped candidates are duplicate editions of a title
already kept for the same year, series volumes without a stated `Kartendaten`
extent, or records without a map year — the comment and `records.json.selection`
state that verbatim. The kept 47 span 1754–1920: the 1754 Zürichsee plan, the
1768–1793 militia exercise plans, the 1804/1852/1866/1867/1880 Breitinger plans,
Oberstrass 1869, the 1871 proposals for the Sihl/rail junction, the 1883
Landesausstellung plan, Uetliberg/Käpfnach/Adlisberg, the 1912 Winterthur district
and the 1920 groundwater maps.

### Measured this iteration (this runner, not copied from a commit message)

- Cold `npm run harvest` (no `.cache/fetch/`): **86 s**, wrote all three files;
  console: “SRU kept 47 Zürich plans of 92 candidates … 169 records, 12 comparison
  layers”. A repeat harvest (warm cache) reproduced the same output in 84 s.
- `npm run build` ✓ (169 records, 2 providers, 12 overlays, 27 with a documented
  depicted period); `npm test` **142/142**; `wrangler deploy --dry-run` ✓.
- Measured seed facts the docs now state: institutions ETH-Bibliothek 68,
  Zentralbibliothek Zürich 65, swisstopo 27, Bern 8, Genf 1; corpora `zut` 65,
  `zuz` 61, `bes_1` 8, `gep_r` 1 (135 of 142 e-rara records have a viewer URL);
  142 shelfmarks; 142 manifests; 169 extents; 27 depicted periods; span 1696–2021.
- `npm run verify:endpoints`: **756 distinct URLs** on the 169-record seed. The
  first run reported 21 failures — all e-rara DOI landing pages answering an
  intermittent **500**; three consecutive hand probes of one of them answered
  200, 200, 500, so they are rate/load artefacts, not dead links. The script now
  retries transient `429/5xx/timeout` a bounded number of times
  (`--retries`, default 2, 600 ms · n backoff) and prints how many URLs needed a
  retry. Re-run with `--concurrency 2 --retries 3`: **756/756, 0 failures** —
  record 169/169, thumbnail 169/169, viewer 135/135, manifest 142/142,
  image-service 141/141; 23 URLs answered a transient 5xx once and 200 on the
  retry. `docs/data-sources.md` and `docs/run.md` state that run.
- Integrated-tree harness (`npx wrangler dev` + `node scripts/browser-check.mjs`)
  on the 169-record seed, after rebasing over maps-2's `242ccb4`: **137/137**,
  no console errors, no failed requests (`/tmp/shots-718b/`). The +29 Zürich plans
  did not break the point filter (56 records at Zürich's centre), the footprints,
  the marker clustering, or the seed-derived harness ids.

### Probes that ended in “keep the seed as it is” (documented, nothing shipped)

- **The region (11) and city-plan (10) SRU sets are pool-limited, not cap-limited.**
  Setting their `perDecade` rule from 3 to 9 leaves both counts exactly unchanged
  (probe run), so their caps stay at 16/14 and their rules are untouched.
- **The world set stays at 21 records.** Pooling all 39 candidates and raising the
  per-decade rule from 3 to 9 adds **two** sheets of decades the set already
  covers (21 → 23, 171 records); not worth a rule change and a re-verification.
- **Swiss cities outside Zürich answer too little** for a fifth set. SRU probes
  (2026-10-19): `dc.title=Plan and dc.subject=Basel` 42 hits (mostly books whose
  title contains “plane”; two real Basel plans with year + coordinates),
  `…=Bern` 28 hits (3 usable), `…=Luzern` 3 hits (1 map, no coordinates),
  `…=Genf`/`Genève` 20/31 hits (a handful, most without `<coordinates>`). A set
  would add ~5 records and a misleading title, so it was not implemented; the
  note lives here instead of in the code.
- **The cantonal geoportal is not usable without credentials.**
  `https://wms.zh.ch/OGDZHWMS?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities` → **401
  “HTTP Basic: Access denied.”** on 2026-10-19 (`maps.zh.ch/wms` → 503,
  `webgis.zh.ch` → no answer); GIS-ZH OGD services are token-based, and the swarm
  must not hold or ship such a token. The canton's historical mapwork is already
  covered through swisstopo's `ch.swisstopo.zeitreihen`/`hiks-*` WMTS layers,
  which are the *same* official raster series with OGD terms — no coverage is
  lost.
- **LoC would need invented coordinates.** The Library of Congress JSON API
  (`https://www.loc.gov/maps/?q=…&fo=json`, CORS `*`) and its IIIF manifests are
  documented and rich, but the item JSON states **no** coordinates for the maps
  probed (e.g. `2005625055`, `2013593105`, `2006629175`): a record could not be
  placed on the map without guessing, so no LoC set was added.

### Messages

- **→ maps-1:** `docs/run.md`'s endpoint row and the harness/record counts in

  untouched. Nothing in your shell files changed this iteration.
- **→ maps-2:** the seed grew by 29 Zürich-area records (many with city-centre

- **→ maps-3:** the harness was run on the 169-record seed: **137/137** (the

  copy or check that says 140/119/113 is stale. The Zürich SRU plan set's rule in

## Iteration 7-16 (2026-10-19, ~00:3x–00:5x UTC) — the world view gets real records

Written up late: this iteration timed out before I recorded it. Its commits are
`8055e95` (data) and the seed they produced; nothing else of that session
survived, so the documentation caught up in 7-17 (below).

### A fourth SRU set: “Übersichtskarten von Europa und der Welt” (21 new records)

Every committed record sat inside the Swiss box, so searching or panning outside
Switzerland found nothing. Six more CQL questions the e-rara catalogue answers
became set `e-rara:sru-world-overview`:

```
dc.subject=Europa  and dc.title=Karte   30 hits
dc.title=Erdkarte / dc.title=Weltkarte  (world maps)
dc.subject=Afrika / Amerika / Asien and dc.title=Karte
```

Same gates as the Zürich SRU sets (map genre, stated year, stated MODS
`<coordinates>`, `GetRecord` + IIIF manifest with a stated holding institution and
`Kartendaten` extent, one entry per title and year, ≤ 3 per publication decade)
plus **two mirrored rules**: the centre of the record's own stated extent must lie
**outside** the canton window (the Zürich sets require inside, so the sets stay
disjoint) and the extent must span **≥ 5°** of latitude or longitude — that is
what separates an overview map from a local sheet. 39 candidates with a stated
extent → 21 kept, 1787–1915, held by ZB Zürich, ETH-Bibliothek and
Universitätsbibliothek Bern. A per-query quota was probed and rejected (only the
Europe query answers many extents, so a quota would have shrunk the set without
adding a continent); the rule is stored verbatim in
`records.json.selection['e-rara:sru-world-overview']`.

Seed: 119 → **140 records** (113 e-rara + 27 swisstopo), e-rara span 1696–1919,
seed span 1696–2021.

## 3. Local fixture provider

The committed registry contains only the two real providers above. Tests that need
synthetic records build them in memory (`tests/records.test.mjs`), so no fixture
metadata can appear in the public data or the UI.

## Fetching policy (politeness, caching, failure behaviour)

- **Bounded harvest**: `scripts/fetch-records.mjs` requests the documented OAI-PMH
  pages (32 `zuz` + 12 `landkarten` + 6 `cartesgeneve` + 6 `museecarto`, with
  resumption tokens), seven SRU pages (seven CQL searches, 100 records each),
  one IIIF manifest and one DOI landing page per candidate title, one
  `GetRecord` confirmation per SRU candidate, and the WMTS
  capabilities document, with a descriptive `User-Agent`
  (`Kartenzeit/1.0 (Canton-Zurich design study; contact: project maintainers)`).
  At most 3 concurrent requests with a short pause between them, and every
  upstream response (including tile probes) is cached under `.cache/fetch/`
  (git-ignored) so `--offline` reproduces the committed data without network
  access; a cold full refresh takes a few minutes, a warm one ~65 s, and the
  harvest is never part of the build.
- **Edge caches in the Worker**: `/api/search/places` 5 minutes,
  `/api/fetch` 1 hour, `/api/records|layers|sources` 5 minutes.
- **Timeouts**: 8 s per upstream call (`AbortSignal.timeout`), abortable client
  fetches in the place search.
- **Allowlist**: literal host + path prefixes only (`src/worker/allowlist.js`);
...... 340-367
`scripts/validate.mjs` and `npm test` are offline by design, so a refresh could
leave a dead link behind without any check noticing. `npm run verify:endpoints`
(`scripts/verify-endpoints.mjs`) is the online counterpart: it reads
`public/data/records.json` and `overlays.json`, collects every distinct URL they
promise (original record, library viewer, thumbnail, IIIF manifest, first-canvas
image service, WMTS preview tile), probes each one once with a descriptive
`User-Agent`, a 20 s timeout and 4 concurrent requests, prints a per-kind summary
and exits non-zero when anything stops answering 200 (`--json <file>` writes the
full report, `--offline` only lists the URLs, `--limit n` probes a prefix).

Last full run — **2026-10-19, 756 distinct URLs, 0 failures** on the 169-record
seed (`--concurrency 2 --retries 3`):

| Kind | Result |
| --- | --- |
| original record (DOI landing page / `map.geo.admin.ch` viewer) | 169/169 |
| thumbnail (IIIF `…/full/304/0/default.jpg` / WMTS tile) | 169/169 |
| library viewer (`…/content/zoom/<id>`) | 135/135 |
| IIIF manifest (`…/i3f/v20/<titleId>/manifest`) | 142/142 |
| IIIF image service (`…/info.json`) | 141/141 |

**Transient 5xx are retried, because e-rara's DOI landing pages throttle.** The
same 169-record seed at `--concurrency 4` reported 21 failures, every one of them
a `record` URL answering **500**; three consecutive hand probes of one of them
answered 200, 200, 500, so they are load artefacts, not dead links. The script
now retries an answer of `429`, `5xx` or a timeout a bounded number of times
(`--retries n`, default 2, with a 600 ms · n backoff) and prints how many URLs
needed the retry; the clean run above needed **23** retries, all of which answered
200 on the second attempt. A future full check should keep the request rate low
(`--concurrency 2`) rather than read a 500 as a dead link.

The script is deliberately *not* part of `npm run check`: the gate stays offline,
hermetic and fast, and this check needs the network.

292:## 3. Local fixture provider

- the centre of the record's own stated extent must lie **outside** the canton
  window (the Zürich sets require the opposite), so one keyword hit can never
  appear in both;
- the extent must span **at least 5°** of latitude or longitude — that is what
  makes a sheet an overview map rather than a local one.

Result: 39 candidates with a stated extent → 21 kept, **1787–1915**, held by ZB
Zürich, ETH-Bibliothek and Universitätsbibliothek Bern (e.g. the 1787
“Carte générale de l'Europe”, the 1830s–1850s “Erdkarte” plates, 19th-century
Africa, America and Asia sheets). The set is skipped entirely when the gazetteer

edits.newText:
Africa, America and Asia sheets). The set is skipped entirely when the gazetteer
is unreachable, like the Zürich sets — the window is not optional. A per-query
quota was probed and rejected: only the Europe query answers many records with a
stated extent, so a quota would have shrunk the set without adding a continent.

### The ETH set becomes a four-century Swiss survey (7-19)

The `landkarten` set states **2335 records**; the seed read the first 12 OAI pages
(120 records) and kept the 50 oldest candidates with a 26-record cap, so its map
was pinned to the 1780s–1830s: the 16th–18th-century Zürich sheets that the same
set holds were simply outside the window. Three bounded changes, no hand-picked
title:

1. **Read 30 pages (300 records) instead of 12** — bounded and documented.
2. **Candidate window** = the 50 oldest candidates of the first 12 pages (the
   window the set was first harvested with, so the deeper read does not lose that
   reach) **∪** 90 candidates evenly spaced over the year-sorted candidates
   (`spreadWindow`, first and last always included) → **125 candidates**, spanning
   the set's whole range instead of its first decades.
3. **Selection** = the union of two documented passes over the candidates that
   state a `Kartendaten` bbox and an upstream year: the **oldest 26** (the
   previous rule, which is where the cantonal and regional sheets outside Zürich
   sit) and a **per-decade spread** (at most 3 records per publication decade, cap
   44), which is the only way the 16th–18th-century material can appear at all.
   Duplicates are still dropped by leading title (60 characters).

Measured result of the harvest: **26 → 56 records** in the set, spanning
**1547–1900** — the 1547 “Das Zürychgow”, 1692 “Geographische … Verzeichnus”,
1698 “Zürich Gebiet”, 1718 “Delineatio aller Quartieren …”, 1738 “Nova et accurata
Agri Tigurini … tabula”, 1766 “Territorium der Republic Zürich”, 1793
“Der Zürich-See …” and the 19th-century cantonal sheets, next to the Atlas Suisse
and Ticino/Vaud/Appenzell material the previous rule already carried. The whole
seed spans **1547–2021** (it was 1696–2021) and grows 169 → **199 records**, while
the non-Zürich Swiss coverage grows 24 → 28 records instead of shrinking (the
per-decade rule alone would have dropped eight of them; the oldest-26 pass keeps
them). Six previously published sheets fall out of the set because the newly
reachable 16th–18th-century sheets take slots in the oldest-26 pass — the rule is
recorded in `records.json.selection['e-rara:landkarten']`, so the churn is
reproducible rather than a surprise.
